interactions.label: A normal mammogram reliably excludes breast cancer in a woman presenting with a

params.question: A normal mammogram reliably excludes breast cancer in a woman presenting with a clinically suspicious breast lump.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: A normal mammogram does not reliably exclude cancer. Dense breast tissue can obscure a malignancy on X-ray, and sensitivity falls in younger women. Triple assessment (clinical examination, imaging, and pathology) ensures that a clinically suspicious lump is never dismissed on the basis of imaging alone.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A normal mammogram cannot rule out cancer, particularly in dense breast tissue where malignancy is easily masked. This is precisely why triple assessment — clinical examination, imaging, and pathology — exists. When clinical and imaging findings disagree, further investigation is mandatory.

params.question: A 32-year-old woman with a confirmed BRCA1 gene mutation presents for breast cancer screening. Which imaging modality is most appropriate as her primary screening tool?

answers.text: Mammography, as it is the standard population screening tool

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Mammography is the standard screening tool for the general population, but its sensitivity drops in the dense breast tissue of younger women. For women at high genetic risk, a more sensitive modality is indicated.

answers.text: Ultrasound, because she is under 40 years of age

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Ultrasound is the first-line choice for symptomatic assessment in young women and for characterising focal lesions, but it is not the recommended primary screening tool for high-risk individuals.

answers.text: Magnetic resonance imaging, as it is indicated for high-risk screening

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MRI offers the highest sensitivity of all breast imaging modalities and is specifically indicated for screening women at high genetic risk, such as BRCA mutation carriers, despite a higher false-positive rate.

answers.text: Computed tomography of the chest for comprehensive breast and thoracic assessment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CT delivers a significant radiation dose and is reserved for staging known malignancy (e.g. detecting lung or liver metastases), not for breast cancer screening.

overallFeedback.feedback: For high-risk screening — particularly in women with a known BRCA gene mutation — MRI is indicated because of its superior sensitivity compared to mammography and ultrasound. Mammography screens the general population; ultrasound characterises symptomatic lesions.

MRI is the modality of choice for breast cancer screening in women at high genetic risk, including BRCA mutation carriers. Its superior sensitivity outweighs the drawback of more frequent false positives in this population.

params.question: A mammogram reveals a well-defined, oval mass with smooth margins and coarse, popcorn-like calcification. Which BI-RADS category is most appropriate?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: BI-RADS 1 denotes a completely normal mammogram with no identifiable finding. Here a mass is clearly present, even though its features are benign.

A well-defined, oval, smooth-margined mass with coarse popcorn-like calcification is the classic mammographic appearance of a fibroadenoma — a definitely benign finding warranting only routine follow-up.

BI-RADS 4 applies to lesions with suspicious features such as irregular margins, spiculation, or fine pleomorphic microcalcifications. Smooth margins and coarse calcification point to a benign aetiology.

BI-RADS 5 is reserved for findings that are classic for malignancy — spiculated masses with fine linear or branching microcalcifications. The features described here are characteristic of a benign fibroadenoma.

overallFeedback.feedback: The combination of smooth margins, oval shape, and coarse popcorn calcification is the classic mammographic appearance of a fibroadenoma. This is a definitely benign finding — BI-RADS 2 — requiring no further workup beyond routine follow-up.

Coarse, popcorn-like calcification within a well-defined oval mass is the hallmark of a fibroadenoma, a definitely benign lesion classified as BI-RADS 2. The management is reassurance and routine screening.

interactions.label: A 26-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant discovers a firm breast lump. Which

params.question: A 26-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant discovers a firm breast lump. Which imaging modality should be used first to evaluate this lump?

answers.text: Mammography, as it is the standard breast imaging tool

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Mammography uses ionising radiation, which should be avoided in pregnancy when a safer alternative exists. Moreover, hormonally stimulated dense breast tissue in pregnancy reduces mammographic sensitivity.

answers.text: MRI with gadolinium contrast for highest sensitivity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Gadolinium crosses the placenta and is generally avoided in pregnancy. MRI is reserved for high-risk screening and staging of confirmed malignancy, not for initial assessment of a palpable lump.

answers.text: Ultrasound, as it is radiation-free and characterises the mass

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Ultrasound carries no ionising radiation, making it safe in pregnancy. It reliably distinguishes solid from cystic masses and is the first-line modality in young women with dense breast tissue. Pregnancy never justifies delaying assessment of a breast lump.

answers.text: CT of the chest for comprehensive evaluation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CT delivers a substantial radiation dose and is used for staging distant metastases in confirmed cancer, not for the initial assessment of a breast lump — especially in pregnancy.

overallFeedback.feedback: In a pregnant woman with a breast lump, ultrasound is the first-line imaging choice. It uses no ionising radiation and characterises masses effectively in dense breast tissue. The finding is then assigned a BI-RADS category to guide management — pregnancy alone never justifies skipping assessment.

Ultrasound is the correct first-line modality: it avoids ionising radiation in pregnancy, performs well in dense breast tissue, and distinguishes solid from cystic masses. The BI-RADS category assigned then determines whether biopsy, follow-up, or reassurance is the next step.
